bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin ASP 2x GB300; $710B combined production value projected
bullets.body: TrendForce projects Vera Rubin's average selling price at twice the GB300, with combined production value of GB300/VR200/VR300 reaching $710B next year—a significant TAM expansion signal for Nvidia's next-gen GPU cycle.

bullets.title: NVDA: Goldman packaging synthetic TRS on hyperscaler credit as CDS widens
bullets.body: Goldman is structuring synthetic total-return swaps on hyperscaler credit as CDS spreads widen: Meta CDS at 75–92bps, Nvidia CDS at 54–82bps with NVDA CDS trading above its own cash bonds—an unusual dislocation flagging credit market stress in mega-cap tech.

bullets.title: NVDA: Implied vol collapsed 32 points overnight; $230 calls were the tell
bullets.body: NVDA implied volatility swung from +10% to -22% in a single session. Fintwit traders flagging the $230 calls as a leading directional signal ahead of the move, worth monitoring for next setup.

bullets.title: NVDA rally on narrow breadth: only 1 of 11 S&P sectors closed green
bullets.body: On the day NVDA melted up, roughly 70% of S&P 500 names declined and only one sector finished positive—underscoring extreme index concentration risk in AI names with the median stock flat.

bullets.title: NVDA denies pause to July business model shift; AI ecosystem demand high
bullets.body: Nvidia reaffirmed its July business model change—providing compute access to the broader AI ecosystem—remains fully active and continues evolving due to high demand, pushing back on bear narratives.

bullets.title: NVDA FY28 revenue forecast raised to 68% growth by Funda
bullets.body: Funda raised its Nvidia FY28 revenue growth forecast to 68% two weeks ago, one of the more bullish sell-side/quant calls in the window.

bullets.title: MRVL -7.8% AH despite solid Q2 beat; FY27E raised to ~$12B
bullets.body: Marvell posted F2Q revenue of $2.74bn (+37% YoY, inline) and non-GAAP EPS $0.94 (slight beat), with F3Q guidance of $3.15bn (+50% YoY). Stock fell 7.8% AH on high expectations; investors await the October Investor Day for next catalyst.

bullets.title: DELL F2Q preview misses: revenue below guidance, AI server raise likely priced in
bullets.body: Dell's F2Q27 revenue seen at $42.2bn vs. $44.5bn guidance midpoint, with EPS $4.70 vs. $4.84 consensus. AI server guidance expected to lift to ~$75bn but the raise is viewed as already in the stock; NVIDIA L72 shipments cut to 17k units.

bullets.title: PYPL crashes ~17% premarket after Advent/Stripe abandon $50B takeover
bullets.body: PayPal shares fell ~17% in premarket after Advent and Stripe walked away from a reported $50 billion takeover bid, removing the M&A premium from the stock.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole: markets laser-focused on Warsh hawkish vs. dovish word choice
bullets.body: Traders flagging that Warsh's language at Jackson Hole will be the key near-term market driver—'hawkish versus dovish words' expected to move rates and equities. Goldman rates trader George Cole also previewed the speech in context of higher long-end rates and the July FOMC.

bullets.title: Global bond yields surge: 10-yr Bund at 15-yr high, French 30-yr at 4.92% (2008 high)
bullets.body: 10-year German Bund yield hit a 15-year high and French 30-year yields rose 3bps to 4.92%—the highest since 2008—ahead of Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks. Japanese 10-yr yields also pressing cycle highs despite record BOJ/MoF intervention.

bullets.title: Japan record FX intervention: $96-98.7B (15.4T yen) deployed in one month to support yen
bullets.body: Japan's Ministry of Finance spent a record 15.4 trillion yen (~$96-98.7B) intervening to support the yen in the month ending August 26, reportedly coordinated with the U.S. USD/JPY still rising 0.2% to 159.64, suggesting intervention is losing ground.

bullets.title: CXMT (Chinese DRAM) posts 873% YoY revenue growth in H1 2026, claims #4 global position
bullets.body: China's CXMT reported H1 2026 revenue of 150.3B yuan vs. 15.44B yuan a year ago (+873% YoY) with net income of 77.6B yuan, claiming fourth-largest DRAM maker status globally—a significant competitive threat to MU and SK Hynix.

bullets.title: BofA Hartnett: stocks fall >10% if Democrats take Senate
bullets.body: Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett warns US equities could drop more than 10% if Democrats gain control of the Senate—a notable political risk flag heading into election season.

bullets.title: Market breadth warning: yesterday's rally came on decelerating volume
bullets.body: Fintwit flagging that the prior session's up day was accompanied by declining trading volume, raising questions about conviction. Bears were wrong on earnings (+52% growth), but with earnings season over markets need a new catalyst.

bullets.title: European gas tops €70/MWh for first time since March 19
bullets.body: European natural gas surged above €70/MWh, the highest level since mid-March, adding to the energy cost pressure narrative for European industry and data centers.

bullets.title: UBS recommends positioning for commodity upcycle; gold back above 200-DMA
bullets.body: UBS is calling for a commodity upcycle driven by global scarcity. Separately, gold reclaimed its 200-day moving average with trend intact and positioning not yet maxed out; silver up 1.8% on the day and +22.3% over the past month.

bullets.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 ramp constrained by UMC 22nm DDI capacity
bullets.body: Korean media reports Samsung is ramping Galaxy Z Fold 8 production on strong demand, but UMC's 22nm capacity producing the display driver ICs is fully utilized, making DDI supply a potential bottleneck.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO could hit $2T valuation—frontier AI lab multiples called 'absurd'
bullets.body: A fintwit observer notes that 10% of a $2T Anthropic IPO valuation could buy several major established consumer brands, questioning whether frontier AI lab valuations have become disproportionate relative to real-world business values.

bullets.title: NVDA's corporate portfolio: ~$30B Intel, ~$21B SpaceX holdings
bullets.body: Fintwit highlighting that Nvidia's investment portfolio has grown to include approximately $30B in Intel securities and $21B in SpaceX equity, illustrating the scale of Nvidia's corporate cash deployment beyond core chip business.
